patch.value: Same-site sibling origins bypass the cookie-authenticated CSRF guard

The custom CSRF middleware protects every state-changing API route, but isCrossSiteRequest treats Sec-Fetch-Site same-site as automatically trusted. A compromised sibling origin such as another unbrained.dev service can send a cookie-authenticated mutation to pm-web; the browser labels it same-site and the current guard allows it before evaluating the mismatched Origin. CodeQL alerts 163 and 164 do not recognize the custom middleware and require evidence-backed false-positive disposition after the real same-site boundary is repaired.

Cookie-authenticated unsafe requests with Sec-Fetch-Site same-site and a foreign Origin are rejected with 403; same-origin requests remain accepted; bearer or non-browser clients without a session cookie retain their documented compatibility; all state-changing API routers remain behind the CSRF middleware; CodeQL alerts 163 and 164 are dispositioned with exact justification; required package gates pass on the exact pushed head.
Reproduced against the real Express middleware with a pm_token cookie, same-site Fetch Metadata, foreign sibling Origin, and a mutating route.
The hosted multi-service origin set shares unbrained.dev, making a sibling-origin compromise a practical CSRF boundary; two high-severity scanner alerts are open on main.

POST through cookieParser and csrfProtection with Cookie pm_token=session, Host pm-web.unbrained.dev, Origin https://evil.unbrained.dev, and Sec-Fetch-Site same-site; the mutation currently returns 204 instead of 403.
Sibling-origin cookie-authenticated mutations are rejected before any route handler runs.
The same-site branch returns false without comparing Origin, so the route executes.
A compromised or attacker-controlled sibling origin can perform authenticated state changes for a visiting pm-web user.

value.text: Greptile exact-head review found a second valid queue lifecycle edge: pm_token lasts 30 days but csrf_token is a browser-session cookie, so a queued record can carry a stale token after restart. TDD changed the replay fixture to include stale-session-token and failed because no bootstrap occurred. The repair now obtains the current token on every non-empty flush, never persists new queue tokens, ignores legacy stored tokens, preserves the full queue if bootstrap fails, and passes the focused 26-test/type/docstring gates.
